title: Efficient Equivariant High-Order Crystal Tensor Prediction via Cartesian Local-Environment Many-Body Coupling
claim: A staged architecture turns raw structure into local environment features, then assembles high-order equivariant outputs through a learnable interaction in channel space.
layout: 3 dashed modules, left-to-right then downward, arrows between rounded blocks
description: A block diagram of the CEITNet architecture, with a green 'Meta data' box on the far left listing lattice parameters (a, b, c; α, β, γ) and atomic sites (Z, x, y, z). A hollow arrow leads into a dashed 'Invariant message passing' module. This module holds a crystal graph construction block, showing a periodic unit cell with atoms turning into a small graph, and a node/edge embedding block with an RBF box and a 'Message passing × L' box. A hollow arrow points down to a dashed 'Local environment construction' module along the bottom. It chains direction encoding, basis construction, and MLP weight generation/pooling, and ends in local environments E_i. A third dashed module on the right, 'Tensor construction', shows an environment interaction grid M ∈ R^{K×K} with highlighted cells linked to two column vectors. Below it are graph pooling, a dotted symmetry adjustment box, and a green output tensor. Blue rounded boxes hold the stages and peach boxes mark learned modules. The eye goes first to the left-hand green input box, then follows the arrows through the stages.
caption: The architecture of CEITNet. It integrates an invariant message passing backbone with a Cartesian-based local environment constructor. The tensor construction head employs a learnable interaction matrix $M$ to capture flexible many-body interactions. Note that some engineering details are omitted in the diagram for clarity.
abstract: End-to-end prediction of high-order crystal tensor properties from atomic structures remains challenging: while spherical-harmonic equivariant models are expressive, their Clebsch-Gordan tensor products incur substantial compute and memory costs for higher-order targets. We propose the Cartesian Environment Interaction Tensor Network (CEITNet), an approach that constructs a multi-channel Cartesian local environment tensor for each atom and performs flexible many-body mixing via a learnable channel-space interaction. By performing learning in channel space and using Cartesian tensor bases to assemble equivariant outputs, CEITNet enables efficient construction of high-order tensor. Across benchmark datasets for order-2 dielectric, order-3 piezoelectric, and order-4 elastic tensor prediction, CEITNet surpasses prior high-order prediction methods on key accuracy criteria while offering high computational efficiency.
